title: The purpose of a static block
answer: A static initialization block runs once when the JVM initializes the class, before ordinary static use proceeds. It is useful when static state needs setup that cannot be expressed cleanly in a single field initializer, although simple field initializers are usually easier to read. AeroTopo's `LanguageLab` has `static { batches = 0; }`, which initializes class-level state. Static blocks should avoid expensive I/O and fragile side effects because initialization failure can make the class unusable.
